Aarhusklyngen is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in Denmark [^src5]. It is one of the many local organizational units monitored by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) in their annual quality reports regarding the treatment and management of [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. 

The cluster is notable for meeting the national quality standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timeliness of initiating anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients, achieving a compliance rate of 92.4% [^src1]. Aarhusklyngen's performance is tracked across a wide array of clinical quality indicators over multiple measurement periods. These include 1-year, 2-year, and 5-year anticoagulation treatment coverage (Indicators 4a1, 4a2, and 4a3) [^src2], as well as the frequency of annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOAC treatment (Indicator 4b) [^src4].

Furthermore, the cluster's data is integral to national epidemiological and outcome tracking. It contributes to the geographic mapping of the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) among atrial fibrillation patients across Danish healthcare clusters [^src4]. The RKKP reports also detail Aarhusklyngen's patient outcomes concerning severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 11) [^src6] and the development of heart failure within the same timeframe (Indicator 15) [^src7]. By providing granular, cluster-level data, Aarhusklyngen helps regional and national health authorities identify variations in clinical practice and benchmark treatment quality across the Danish healthcare system.
